title: Frequency-uniform squared boundary observation of quadratic Kolmogorov equations from short early observation windows
difficulty_reason: H3: the existing variable-potential resolvent theorem alone does not yield boundary observation uniform in all Fourier modes. The authors design two one-sided nonlinear Carleman phases with sqrt(n) scaling, match their constants at the degeneracy, absorb the cutoff commutators in an overlap, and keep the maximal action integral as the leading exponential observation cost. They then balance that cost against the sharp-in-rate nonselfadjoint semigroup decay from the existing resolvent core, include the finitely many low modes and use Fourier/Parseval reconstruction. This produces the exact terminal-state inequality on arbitrarily short permitted early windows with a constant independent of the Fourier mode. The complete spectral/Carleman/dissipation mechanism is a research-level proof obligation; the primary is the authors explicitly squared Proposition2.4, not a repaired interpretation of the introductory norm-power definition.
